source_text: CAPUT DECIMUM QUINTUM, De ministerio verbi. MINISTERIUM VERBI quod est officium sacrum a Deo per legitimam vocationem idoneis personis iniunctum, ut verbum ipsius docendo, sacramenta administrando, absolvendo et ligando, homines ad regnum Dei ac salutem vocent atque dirigant. Graecis diakonia dicitur (Acts 1:17; 6:4); item leitourgia (Phil. 2:17; Rom. 15:16); episkope (Acts 1:20; 1 Tim. 3:1); oikonomia (1 Cor. 9:17; Eph. 3:2). In V.T. ministerium Levitarum dicitur custodia et militia. Patres vocant hierurgiam; quo sensu Paulo ministri sunt presbyteroi (1 Tim. 5:17). Est officium sacrum (1 Tim. 3:1) distinctum a profanis et civilibus (Matt. 26:21; Luke 22:25).
english: CHAPTER FIFTEEN. On the ministry of the word.

The MINISTRY OF THE WORD is a sacred office enjoined by God through lawful calling on fit persons, that by teaching His word, administering the sacraments, and absolving and binding, they may call and direct people to God's kingdom and salvation.

In Greek it is called diakonia, leitourgia, episkope, oikonomia; in the Old Testament the Levites' ministry is custody and warfare. The Fathers call it hierurgia; Paul names ministers presbyteroi. It is a sacred office distinct from profane and civil offices.

source_text: Eius causa princeps efficiens est Deus (Ps. 68:12; 1 Cor. 12:28; Matt. 9:38), et Spiritus Sanctus ipse loquitur per prophetas. Proxima causa est vocatio divina (Heb. 5:4), alias missio (Rom. 10:14), electio (Luke 6:13). Estque alia immediata, alia mediata. Immediata seu extraordinaria est, cum Deus quosdam peculiari mandato instructos non accedente hominum electione mittit—in V.T. patriarchas et prophetas, in N.T. Apostolos. Mediata et ordinaria est, quae fit per media divinitus constituta, per quae a Deo ut causa principe dirigitur (Num. 3:11; 2 Chron. 29:11; Eph. 4:11; Acts 20:28).
english: Its chief efficient cause is God, and the Holy Spirit Himself speaks through the prophets. The proximate cause is divine calling—also named mission or election—either immediate or mediate.

Immediate or extraordinary calling is when God sends some by His peculiar mandate without human election (patriarchs, prophets, Apostles). Mediate and ordinary calling runs through means God constituted, directed by Him as principal cause.

source_text: Medium vocationis ordinariae est electio Ecclesiae legitima. Deus ecclesiae suae dedit claves regni caelorum (Matt. 16:18; 18:17) verbumque et sacramenta concredidit. Quapropter ecclesia Dei eligit et vocat ministros per tres ordines: (1) presbyterii sive pastorum ecclesiae (Acts 14:23; 1 Tim. 4:14; Tit. 1:5); (2) magistratuum, qui sunt membra ecclesiae et nutritii (Isa. 49:23); (3) populi Christiani (Acts 6:3; 14:23; 1 Cor. 16:3). Quales personae eligendae sint docet Paulus (1 Tim. 3; Tit. 1): communia—fideles, irreprehensibiles, sobrii, hospitales, iusti; propria—apti ad docendum, tenaces sanae doctrinae, potentes exhortari et contradicentes refellere, non neophyti.
english: The means of ordinary calling is the Church's lawful election. God gave His church the keys of the kingdom and entrusted word and sacraments; therefore the church elects ministers through three orders: the eldership or pastors; magistrates as nursing fathers; and the Christian people.

Paul teaches the requisites (1 Tim. 3; Tit. 1): common—faithful, blameless, sober, hospitable, just; proper to the office—apt to teach, holding sound doctrine, able to exhort and refute opponents, not neophytes.

source_text: Forma ministerii in tribus potissimum consistit: (1) in officio docendi et praedicandi verbum (Matt. 28:19; Mark 16:15)—hinc ministri doctores, legati Dei, operarii in verbo; (2) in officio administrandi sacramenta secundum Christi institutionem (Matt. 28:19)—dispensatores mysteriorum Dei (1 Cor. 4:1); (3) in officio remittendi peccata resipiscentibus ac ligandi non resipiscentes, quae dicitur excommunicatio (Matt. 18:18; 16:19), generatim in concionibus et speciatim ad singulas personas, fine ut in Dei gloriam homines serventur.
english: The form of the ministry consists chiefly in three parts. First comes teaching and preaching the word; hence ministers are teachers, ambassadors of God, and laborers in the word.
Second comes administering the sacraments according to Christ's institution; ministers are stewards of the mysteries of God.

Third comes remitting sins to the repentant and binding the unrepentant, which is called excommunication, whether generally in sermons or specially toward persons, so that people may be saved unto the glory of God.

source_text: II. Regulae: 1. Deus non privatis suggestionibus cum scripto verbo pugnantibus, sed ministerio verbi et sacramentorum salutem efficaciter operatur (Acts 9; 10). 2. Omnes Christiani verbum tractare et propagare debent; nemo tamen publice in Ecclesia docere et sacramenta administrare potest nisi specialiter et legitime vocatus—excepto casu necessitatis. 3. Vocatio immediata hodie nec quaeri nec expectari debet (Eph. 4:11). 4. Ministerium non otiosa dignitas sed arduum munus. 5-11. Vocatio non solius presbyterii; ordines diversi; errores refellendi sine putaminibus; visitationes; disciplina—privata monitione, publica correptione, excommunicatio ultimo remedio. CAPUT DECIMUM SEXTUM sequitur, De fide.
english: II. Rules: God works salvation not by private suggestions against Scripture but by the ministry of word and sacraments. All Christians must handle and spread the word, yet none may publicly teach and administer sacraments unless specially and lawfully called—save a case of necessity.

Immediate calling is neither to be sought nor expected today. The ministry is not idle dignity but an arduous office. Call is not of the eldership alone; diverse orders stand; errors must be refuted without chasing obsolete husks; visitations and discipline proceed from private admonition to public rebuke, excommunication only as last resort.
